name: IL-10
label: Safe D

key_factors: Strong Democratic district with a +12 partisan lean
Well-funded incumbent Schneider with $1.7M on hand
Republican challenger has no reported fundraising
Prediction markets price Democratic win at ~96%
model.rationale: Schneider is a well-funded incumbent in a district with a +12 Democratic lean, while Lambrecht shows no reported fundraising or outside support. Markets price a Democratic win near 96%, consistent with a Safe D rating.
model.watch: A major polling miss or unexpected late outside spending against Schneider would be the main signal of movement.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Brad Schneider seeks another term in a northern Illinois district that leans Democratic by about twelve points. He enters the general election with roughly $1.7 million on hand and no outside spending against him, while Republican Carl Lambrecht has no reported fundraising or cash on hand. No public polls cover the race, and no expert raters have flagged it as competitive.

Prediction markets give Schneider about a 96% chance of winning, and the fundamentals point to a comfortable margin in the low twenties. The forecast calls this Safe D, with the incumbent heavily favored and little evidence of a serious challenge.
